items.title: NASA's Artemis II moon mission set to launch Wednesday

featured_image.name: Victor Glover Artemis II Crew Announcement Resource Reel

items.description: NASA is hours away from launching the first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century, with Navy Captain Victor Glover at the controls. The Artemis II mission is scheduled to lift off on Wednesday, April 1, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, sending four astronauts on an approximately 10-day journey around the moon and back.[1][2]

items.title: Indonesia rations fuel as Iran war drives oil prices higher

featured_image.name: Indonesia fuel rations amid Middle East war | The Straits Times

items.description: Indonesia announced fuel rationing on Tuesday as the month-old US-Israel military campaign against Iran continues to choke global energy supplies, with Brent crude trading above $100 a barrel and no diplomatic resolution in sight.

items.title: Trump warns European allies after Italy, France block US military access

featured_image.name: Trump lashes out at UK and France, telling allies 'the U.S.A. won't be there to help you anymore'

items.description: A widening rift between the United States and its European allies deepened on Tuesday as Italy and France took steps to block American military operations from their territory, prompting President Donald Trump to warn that "the USA won't be there to help you anymore." The escalating dispute over European involvement in the month-old US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is straining the NATO alliance while a parallel energy crisis rattles the continent's economy.

items.title: France denies blocking US military overflights after Trump threatens 'USA will remember'

featured_image.name: Trump hits out at France for closing airspace during Iran war

items.description: French officials on Tuesday rejected President Donald Trump's assertion that Paris had blocked American military planes from crossing its airspace, clarifying that its overflight policy for U.S. aircraft remains unchanged even as it acknowledged refusing a specific weekend request to transport weapons to Israel.

items.title: China verifies Mach 6 engine prototype after 30 years

featured_image.name: China's hypersonic jet shatters Mach 6.5 speed in Gobi desert test

items.description: Chinese researchers have completed and experimentally verified a prototype of a novel air-breathing propulsion system that can accelerate from a dead stop to more than six times the speed of sound, according to a report by the South China Morning Post on Sunday. The engine, called the "contra-rotary ramjet," represents over three decades of development and could reshape the design of future fighter jets and hypersonic missiles.[1][2][3]

items.title: Fourth Greek tanker crosses Hormuz despite Iran blockade

featured_image.name: Oil tanker transits Hormuz in rare voyage after Iran war disruption

items.description:
The Greek-controlled Suezmax tanker Pola has successfully crossed the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the fourth vessel managed by Athens-based Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. to navigate the chokepoint since the US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on February 28, according to Bloomberg.[1]

The Pola switched off its Automatic Identification System in the Persian Gulf on March 10 and reappeared on Monday in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia's Sumatra island, vessel tracking data compiled by Bloomberg showed. The tanker, laden with roughly 1 million barrels of crude, is en route to Thailand, according to intelligence firm Kpler.[1]

items.title: King Charles confirms first US state visit as monarch

featured_image.name: King Charles to address Congress in historic first state ... - Fox News

items.description:
Buckingham Palace announced on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will undertake a state visit to the United States in late April, marking the first trip to America by a British monarch since Queen Elizabeth II's visit in 2007.[1][2]

The visit, made at the invitation of President Donald Trump and on the advice of the British government, will celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence — a milestone with particular resonance given that the U.S. declared independence during the reign of Charles's ancestor King George III.[2]

items.title: U.S., Israel strike Isfahan and Tehran on Day 32 of Iran war

featured_image.name: Pakistan says it will host US-Iran talks after diplomats ... - AP News

items.description: As the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran entered its 32nd day on Tuesday, powerful explosions rocked both Tehran and the central city of Isfahan in what appeared to be some of the most intense aerial bombardments since hostilities began on February 28. The escalation came alongside fresh Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region and a parallel diplomatic push led by Pakistan to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.[1][2]

items.title: Trump tells allies to 'take' Strait of Hormuz themselves

featured_image.name: Trump criticizes allies who aren't helping secure the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his pressure on reluctant allies on Tuesday, posting on Truth Social that countries struggling with jet fuel shortages caused by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz should either purchase American oil or seize control of the waterway themselves.

"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you: Number 1, buy from the US, we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT," Trump wrote, singling out nations that declined to join U.S. strikes against Iran. He added that the United States "won't be there to help you anymore" and that allies would need to learn "how to fight for yourself".[1][2][3]

items.title: Hegseth calls upcoming days 'decisive' in Iran war

featured_image.name: Iran War Live Updates: Pete Hegseth holds Pentagon briefing as Iran war intensifies

items.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday described the "upcoming days" as decisive in the month-long U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, pointing to widespread desertions within Tehran's armed forces and the degradation of its military capabilities as signs that the conflict is approaching a turning point.[1][2]

items.title: Global banks turn to Chinese stocks as Iran war roils markets

featured_image.name: Chinese stock market rallying on Thursday with Shanghai ...

items.description: As the month-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran roils global markets and sends oil prices soaring, Chinese equities — and the country's dominant renewable energy sector in particular — have emerged as a rare bright spot for investors seeking refuge from the turmoil.

items.title: Australia, Indonesia probe tech giants over under-16 bans

featured_image.name: Why is Australia banning social media for teenagers?

items.description: Australia and Indonesia are both cracking down on major technology companies this week for failing to enforce new laws banning children under 16 from social media, in a coordinated global push to hold platforms accountable for youth safety online.

items.title: Gold climbs on report Trump may end Iran war

featured_image.name: Gold losses ease as Trump postpones Iran energy strikes - CNBC

items.description: Gold prices climbed on Monday after a Wall Street Journal report that President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the U.S. military campaign against Iran, even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. The gains extended into early Asian trading on Tuesday, with the metal also buoyed by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's comments at Harvard University that eased fears of an imminent interest rate hike.

items.title: Data centers warm nearby land by up to 16°F, Cambridge study finds

featured_image.name: Space-based thermal maps reveal urban heat islands and how ...

items.description: The sprawling data centers powering artificial intelligence are creating localized "heat islands" that raise surface temperatures by an average of 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit — and up to 16.4 degrees in extreme cases — affecting an estimated 340 million people worldwide, according to new research from the University of Cambridge.

items.title: Asian nations rush to buy Russian crude as Iran war chokes oil supply

featured_image.name: Russian oil arrives as Philippines battles 'energy emergency'

items.description:
A growing number of Asian countries are turning to Russia for crude oil as the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran continues to choke off energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."[1][2]

The Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka have all signaled interest in purchasing Russian crude in recent weeks, joining established buyers China and India in a regional competition for barrels that analysts warn may soon outstrip what Moscow can deliver.[3][4]

items.title: Trump willing to end Iran war without reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: White House: Reopening Strait of Hormuz Not Vital to Ending Iran War

items.description:
President Donald Trump has told aides he is willing to conclude the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial shipping, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, a move that could leave Tehran with lasting leverage over one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.[1]

The shift signals a recalibration of American war aims as the conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, enters its fifth week. In recent discussions, Trump and his advisers concluded that attempting to force the strait open would extend the fighting beyond his preferred four-to-six-week timeline, according to administration officials cited by the Journal. Instead, Washington plans to focus on its stated objectives — degrading Iran's naval and missile capabilities — while pursuing diplomatic channels to persuade Tehran to restore maritime traffic.[1]

items.title: US struck Isfahan ammo depot with bunker busters

featured_image.name: Iran War News: Massive Blasts In Iran's Isfahan After US-Israeli Strikes,  Trump Shares Video

items.description:
The United States struck a large ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan with a high volume of 2,000-pound penetrator munitions, according to a U.S. official cited by The Wall Street Journal. The strike triggered a chain of secondary explosions that lit up the night sky, with footage of towering fireballs circulating widely after President Trump shared an uncaptioned video of the attack on his Truth Social platform on Sunday evening. The Wall Street Journal confirmed the footage depicted the Isfahan operation.[1][2][3]

The strike is the latest in more than a month of sustained U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, launched on February 28 under what the Israel Defense Forces have termed "Operation Roaring Lion". Since then, more than 15,000 Iranian targets have been hit, according to the IDF, with the daily strike tempo declining from roughly 1,000 targets in the opening days to fewer than 100.[4][5][6]

items.title: Iran says ambassador will stay in Beirut despite Lebanon's expulsion order

featured_image.name: Iran Says Envoy Will Remain in Beirut Despite Lebanon Order to ...

items.description:
Iran on Monday openly refused to comply with Lebanon's order to expel its ambassador, declaring that the envoy would remain in Beirut and continue his duties — a direct challenge to the Lebanese government's authority that has deepened a diplomatic crisis at the heart of the broader regional conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei confirmed at a news conference that Ambassador Mohammad Reza Shibani had no plans to leave. "Our embassy is open and our ambassador continues his work in Beirut and remains present," Baghaei said, according to Iran International. The statement came one day after a March 29 deadline set by Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi for Shibani to depart the country.[1][2][3]

items.title: NYU closes Abu Dhabi campus after Iran threatens US universities

featured_image.name: Overview - NYU Abu Dhabi

items.description:
New York University has temporarily shut down its Abu Dhabi campus after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared American university outposts in the Middle East "legitimate targets" for retaliation, marking a sharp escalation that extends the ongoing conflict into the realm of civilian academic institutions.

The closure, announced on Monday, suspends physical access to the campus for all students, faculty, and staff, with classes continuing remotely, according to NYU's student newspaper, Washington Square News. The university said the decision was made "out of an abundance of caution" following the IRGC's threat on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Kuwaiti oil tanker hit by projectile near Dubai port

featured_image.name: Kuwait says its giant crude oil tanker Al-Salmi was directly targeted by an  Iranian attack while anchored in the anchorage area of Dubai Port, UAE. The  tanker was fully loaded at the

items.description:
A fully loaded Kuwaiti crude oil tanker was struck by a projectile while anchored near Dubai port early on Tuesday, March 31, sparking a fire onboard and raising fears of an oil spill in the Persian Gulf, according to Kuwait's state news agency and a British maritime monitoring authority.

Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said the very large crude carrier Al Salmi was "directly targeted in what it described as an Iranian attack while in the anchorage area of Dubai Port in the United Arab Emirates," the state news agency KUNA reported, as cited by Reuters. The corporation warned of a possible oil spill in surrounding waters, adding that the tanker was fully loaded at the time of the strike. No crew casualties were reported, and emergency response and firefighting teams were mobilized to contain the situation.[1]
